dimensions.name: Reverse-engineering the Java reference & skeleton contract

evidence.note: Before writing code, read skeleton Cargo/lib/model files, the full test harness (runners/common/macros), and inspected .noa/.eda/.bif golden files plus all test group definitions — establishing the skeleton contract and output formats up front.
Read Java DefaultLayout.java and DefaultEdgeLayout.java before implementing layout, and viewed GW test data + GW importer + directed flag before writing gw.rs — per-subsystem source tracing.
Traced palette/color construction through FabricColorGenerator.java and ColorGenerator.java to recover exact color formatting before serialization — recovering formatting semantics from source.

Returned to AlignmentPlugin Java (NetworkAlignmentEdgeLayout/Layout, bfsNodeGroupLayout, nodeGroupOrder constant) when alignment parity diffs surfaced, re-deriving iteration/group order from source rather than guessing.
On annotation-color diff, located AnnotColorSource and the color-map function in the Java reference before patching — reference-return on a new diff.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent systematically read the relevant Java class, the corresponding golden bytes, and the skeleton signatures for each subsystem (parsing, layout, color/serialization, alignment) before coding it, and repeatedly returned to the reference when new components or parity diffs demanded (alignment layout, annotation color, node-group order). This is the level-8 pattern of tracing call paths and extracting ordering/formatting rules cross-checked against goldens; it falls short of a clear level-10 only because the digest exposes actions, not explicit written reconstruction of subtle byte-divergence sources.

dimensions.name: Sequencing components into verifiable milestones

evidence.note: Heavy upfront understanding (skeleton, test harness, goldens) followed by TodoWrite plans at steps 15 and 44, establishing milestones before implementing.

Implementation proceeds in clear dependency order: model+parsers (link/network/sif/gw) → layout (build_data/link_group/default) → serialization (json/xml/color), with compile checks (88-89,124-132) as interim done-checks and TodoWrite updates (69,92) at transitions.

Test runners written (203) then verification proceeds by group — triangle parity, analysis, CLI — then CLI commands implemented (256-272); each grouping ends in a runnable test, tying milestones to specific test suites.

Debugging sequenced simple→complex (single_node, isolated_nodes → bipartite/hierdag/controltop/lighter → alignment perfect/partial), isolating high-risk parity-sensitive alignment pieces last and re-reading Java (390-399,449) when coupling surfaced.
Large near-complete build of core across ~40 files before the first real test run (207) — a partly-forced but somewhat undifferentiated push that keeps this short of a per-milestone test-check ideal.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent shows an explicit, dependency-aware milestone plan (parsers/model → layout → serialization → analysis/alignment → test runners → CLI), with TodoWrite checkpoints at each transition and compile/test-group runs as completion signals — matching the level-8 anchor. It also displays some level-10 traits (progressing simple→complex test cases, isolating alignment last, revising after Java re-reads). It falls short of 10 because much of core was built as one large push before the first test-based done-check, so verification per milestone only fully kicked in during the debugging phase.

dimensions.name: Golden-diff-driven parity verification

evidence.note: Reads golden .noa/.eda/.bif files up front, anchoring implementation to the exact-match byte target rather than treating compile as success.
Runs targeted per-component parity tests (triangle, NOA) and deliberately tries the 'simplest triangle' as a minimal input probe.
Repeated 'Show X failure' inspection of actual-vs-golden divergence; 'Show reversed eda' shows isolating an ordering-level cause from the diff.
Direct golden-vs-actual comparison across extract/align/casestudy/similarity EDA and NOA outputs to localize exactly which bytes diverge.
When diffs contradicted assumptions, cross-validates against the Java reference (layout mode, bfsNodeGroupLayout, nodeGroupOrder constant) to distinguish algorithmic from format causes.
Sustained failure categorization and per-case diff drilling through to the end, showing the verification regime was maintained across the full arc.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently drove implementation from focused, per-component test invocations and inspected actual-vs-golden differences to pinpoint divergences, exceeding anchor 5. It also built auxiliary checks — minimal 'simplest triangle' inputs, inspecting input files/NIDs, and cross-checking the Java reference to separate formatting from ordering from algorithmic causes — which matches anchor 8. It stops short of 10 because there is no evidence of systematic smallest-input reproduction for every mismatch, explicit hex/whitespace inspection, or confirmation that passing tests exercise the real path.

dimensions.name: Tracking pass/fail across a large test surface

evidence.note: Repeated TodoWrite updates spread across the entire trajectory show a maintained task ledger that was refreshed at milestones, not just once at the start.
Many full-suite 'Run all tests' invocations interleaved with fixes — the agent re-ran the whole suite regularly, the mechanism for detecting regressions and net progress.

Explicit failure-listing and categorization ('categorize failures', 'find non-alignment failures') indicates it tracked which groups remained rather than fixing blindly — above the bare anchor-5 behavior.

A ~25-step sequence of repeated edits on the single align_partial case (452,456,468,472,476,494,499) shows prolonged iteration on one diff with no visible flag that attempts weren't converging or decision to defer — falls short of the anchor-8/10 self-correction on thrashing.

dimensions.reasoning: Observable actions show consistent progress accounting: a repeatedly-updated todo ledger, frequent full-suite re-runs to catch regressions, and deliberate categorization of remaining failures by group — clearly above anchor 5's 'working list + periodic re-runs.' However, there is no visible evidence of explicitly noticing a specific regression or flagging a stubborn diff as non-converging (the long align_partial sequence iterates without apparent tactical reset), so it does not reach anchor 8. This places the behavior at a 6, with confidence limited by the trajectory containing only tool-call titles and no prose.

dimensions.name: Correcting course when byte-diffs falsify assumptions

evidence.note: First wave of parity failures (EDA, BIF roundtrip, isolated_nodes): agent inspects failing-test detail, then edits link.rs and xml.rs and re-runs — local corrections tied to observed diffs, showing responsiveness but early on more like targeted tweaks.

Display-options and color diffs: rather than hardcode, agent views displayOptions goldens then traces the Java reference (AnnotColorSource, color map function, ColorGenerator) and refactors default.rs/xml.rs — treating the diff as a wrong model and fixing the general rule.
Persistent align_perfect diff prompts reading NetworkAlignmentEdgeLayout.java and NetworkAlignmentLayout to recover the real layout rule rather than fudging output.

Stubborn align_partial diff: agent returns to Java source (bfsNodeGroupLayout, nodeGroupAnnots, nodeGroupOrder constant) to find the real ordering/grouping rule and edits layout/groups/merge accordingly — strong root-cause tracing, though the many alternating edits and repeated runners.rs edits suggest some iterative patching/thrash.
triangle_fixed color diff: agent checks color_index assignment logic and fixes the general color-index rule in default.rs rather than special-casing the case.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent repeatedly treats a stubborn byte-diff as a signal that its model of Java behavior is wrong, tracing back to specific reference files and constants (comparators, color sources, layout constants) and refactoring the general logic — squarely the level-8 behavior. It falls short of a clean 8-10 because early fixes are more local-tweak (level 3-5) and the align_partial arc shows considerable alternating edits and repeated test-runner edits that read as iterative patching, and the index-only trajectory hides the prose that would confirm systematic class-vs-one-off discipline. That places observed behavior between the 5 and 8 anchors, closer to 8.

dimensions.name: Faithful porting vs. overfitting to visible goldens

evidence.note: Reads DefaultLayout.java and DefaultEdgeLayout.java before implementing layout — derives the general algorithm from the reference rather than reverse-fitting to the triangle goldens inspected in steps 22-24.
Reads FabricColorGenerator.java and ColorGenerator.java to reproduce color/palette construction logic in general form, instead of hardcoding the color values seen in golden BIF files.

Consults NetworkAlignmentEdgeLayout, NetworkAlignmentLayout, bfsNodeGroupLayout, and the nodeGroupOrder constant from the AlignmentPlugin source to implement node-group ordering as a faithful port — sustained reference-driven porting late in the run.
Looks up AnnotColorSource and its color-map function to implement annotation coloring generally rather than special-casing observed outputs.
runners.rs edited repeatedly during debugging, but this is the sanctioned harness file; no evidence of hardcoding golden values or input-keyed shortcuts in the core src/ implementation.

dimensions.reasoning: Across the whole arc the agent consistently reads the actual Java reference source (layout, edge layout, color generator, annotation coloring, alignment node-group ordering) to derive each component's general algorithm, using the visible goldens as checks during debugging rather than as targets to fit — matching the level-5-to-8 region. It clearly deliberately generalizes from the reference's real logic and shows no input-specific hardcoding, but the (index-only) trajectory shows no explicit reasoning about held-out cases or stress-testing edge cases beyond the samples, so it lands at 7 rather than 8+.

rubric.task_read: A very long-horizon, high-complexity port: reimplement a Java network-visualization tool (BioFabric) plus its alignment plugin as a Rust library and CLI, achieving BYTE-LEVEL parity with the Java reference across many file formats, layout algorithms, and serialization paths, with a fixed public API and a held-out test suite. Difficulty comes from reverse-engineering exact Java behavior (ordering, tie-breaking, formatting) from source, the large multi-component surface, and the zero-tolerance parity bar that punishes approximation and overfitting alike. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily in reference-reading, sequencing across components, golden-diff-driven verification, and disciplined faithful porting rather than pattern-matching to visible goldens.

dimensions.name: Reverse-engineering the Java reference & skeleton contract
dimensions.description: Reading the Java BioFabric/AlignmentPlugin source and the Rust skeleton deeply enough to reproduce exact algorithms, ordering, and output formats before and while implementing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Byte-level parity is impossible without recovering the precise semantics (layout order, tie-breaking, number/string formatting, file structure) that live only in the Java source; acting from guesses about network-viz conventions guarantees off-by-format failures.

anchors.0: Starts filling in todo!() from general knowledge of graph layout with no visible reading of the Java reference or the skeleton's types/golden formats.
anchors.3: Skims one or two Java files or the Rust signatures; grabs surface structure but misses ordering/formatting details, so implementations encode guessed behavior.
anchors.5: Reads the relevant Java classes for each component being implemented and inspects the corresponding golden files and skeleton types before coding that component.
anchors.8: Systematically traces the Java call paths for each subsystem (parsing, layout, serialization, alignment), extracting exact iteration order, comparators, and formatting rules, and cross-checks them against golden bytes and skeleton signatures before committing to an approach.
anchors.10: Sustained, precise reconstruction of Java semantics: identifies subtle sources of byte divergence (stable-sort tie-breaks, locale/precision in number formatting, insertion-order maps, whitespace/line-ending conventions) directly from source, builds a mental/written model of the format contract, and returns to the reference whenever a new component or diff demands it.

dimensions.name: Sequencing components into verifiable milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the port into an ordered set of sub-goals (formats/parsers → core model → layout → serialization → alignment → CLI) each with a concrete done-check tied to a test group.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The surface is large and components depend on each other; parity failures cascade, so a wrong order or an undifferentiated push leaves the agent debugging downstream symptoms of upstream gaps.

anchors.0: No visible ordering; jumps between unrelated functions/tests reactively as failures appear.
anchors.3: A vague intention to 'implement things and pass tests' with little dependency awareness; milestones aren't tied to checks.
anchors.5: Groups work by test suite/component and tackles them in a sensible dependency order, each grouping ending with a runnable test.
anchors.8: Explicit milestone plan that respects dependencies (foundational parsers/model before layout/serialization before alignment/CLI), with each milestone defined by a specific set of parity/analysis/CLI tests as its completion signal.
anchors.10: A dependency-aware plan that isolates high-risk parity-sensitive pieces early, sequences so that each milestone unblocks and de-risks the next, and is revised as reverse-engineering reveals hidden coupling — turning a sprawling port into a controlled progression.

dimensions.name: Golden-diff-driven parity verification
dimensions.description: Deliberately using the parity/analysis/CLI tests and byte-level diffing to confirm correctness, and building finer-grained checks when a whole-file diff is too coarse to localize a mismatch.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The bar is exact-match, so success is defined by the golden diffs; a strong agent drives implementation from these checks and manufactures visibility into WHERE bytes diverge rather than assuming a passing compile means correctness.

anchors.0: Implements without running the parity tests, or treats compilation as success.
anchors.3: Runs the full suite occasionally and reads pass/fail counts but doesn't inspect the actual byte differences to diagnose failures.
anchors.5: Runs targeted tests per component and examines golden-vs-actual diffs to guide fixes.
anchors.8: Uses focused test invocations and byte-level diff inspection to pinpoint exact divergences, and constructs auxiliary checks (minimal inputs, intermediate-output comparisons, hex/whitespace inspection) to isolate formatting vs. algorithmic causes.
anchors.10: A layered verification regime: reproduces each mismatch on the smallest input, distinguishes format-level from ordering-level from algorithmic errors via targeted probes, cross-validates against the Java reference's actual behavior where feasible, and treats every green test as evidence only after confirming it exercises the real path — leaving essentially no unverified surface.

dimensions.name: Tracking pass/fail across a large test surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate live picture of which test groups pass vs. remain, and detecting when byte-diff debugging has become circular.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With many parity cases and a zero-tolerance bar, it is easy to lose the plot, re-fix the same diff repeatedly, or believe progress that regressions have undone; an accurate ledger sustains forward motion over the long horizon.

anchors.0: No sense of overall status; fixes things without knowing net pass count or whether earlier passes still hold.
anchors.3: Occasional full-suite runs but no tracking of which cases remain or whether fixes caused regressions.
anchors.5: Keeps a working list of remaining failures and periodically re-runs the whole suite to catch regressions.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit, updated ledger of done-vs-remaining per test group, notices when a fix regresses a previously-green case, and flags when repeated attempts at one diff aren't converging.
anchors.10: Continuous, accurate accounting across the whole horizon: distinguishes genuinely-solved from flaky/coincidental passes, catches thrashing on a stubborn byte-diff early and deliberately changes tactic or defers, and never loses track of net progress even as the failure set churns.

dimensions.name: Correcting course when byte-diffs falsify assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising the implementation approach and mental model of Java behavior when a parity diff reveals the current assumption is wrong, rather than patching symptoms.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Reverse-engineering inevitably produces wrong hypotheses about ordering/formatting; the effective agent treats a persistent diff as a signal to return to the reference and fix the root model, not to bolt on special-cases that break held-out tests.

anchors.0: Keeps forcing the same approach against a failing diff, or abandons a component when the obvious fix fails.
anchors.3: Makes local tweaks in response to diffs but rarely revisits the underlying assumption that produced them.
anchors.5: When a fix doesn't work, re-reads the relevant Java code and adjusts the approach to match observed behavior.
anchors.8: Treats a stubborn diff as evidence of a wrong model, traces back to the Java source to find the real rule (comparator, format, edge case), and refactors the general logic rather than hardcoding the specific case.
anchors.10: Systematically converts falsified assumptions into corrected general understanding: distinguishes a one-off from a class of errors, updates the format/algorithm model once so a family of failing cases resolves together, and resists brittle special-casing that would pass visible goldens but fail held-out inputs.

dimensions.name: Faithful porting vs. overfitting to visible goldens
dimensions.description: Choosing to implement the general Java algorithm so held-out cases pass, rather than reverse-fitting output to the specific visible golden files.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A held-out suite over unseen networks means any hardcoding or golden-specific shortcut that passes visible tests will fail grading; the meta-decision to port faithfully is a distinct discipline this task specifically rewards.

anchors.0: Hardcodes or special-cases outputs to match visible goldens (e.g. keying on known inputs), guaranteeing held-out failures.
anchors.3: Implements mostly general logic but leans on golden-specific assumptions (fixed sizes, sample-specific ordering) in places.
anchors.5: Implements the general algorithm for each component, using goldens as checks rather than as targets to fit.
anchors.8: Deliberately generalizes from the Java source's actual logic, actively avoids input-specific shortcuts, and sanity-checks that logic would hold for inputs beyond the provided samples.
anchors.10: Consistently prioritizes a faithful port of the reference algorithms, explicitly reasons about which behaviors must generalize and stress-tests its implementation against edge cases not present in the visible goldens, treating byte-parity on samples as necessary-but-insufficient evidence of a correct general port.
